Solve an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the 74-bus distribution system model `case74ds`. Before running the OPF, modify the network data as follows:

1) At bus 5, tighten the lower bound on the voltage magnitude by setting the minimum allowable voltage magnitude VMIN to 0.99 per unit, so the bus voltage cannot drop below 0.99 p.u. in the optimization.

2) For all generators connected at bus 10, modify their quadratic generation cost characteristics by scaling the cubic (third-order) active power cost coefficient (the C3 term in the polynomial cost function) by a factor of 0, effectively setting that highest-order cost coefficient to zero. This removes the cubic dependence of operating cost on active power for generators at bus 10, leaving only lower-order terms (if present) in their cost functions.

3) For the transmission line (or distribution feeder) that directly connects bus 14 and bus 70, adjust the total line charging susceptance by scaling the branch shunt susceptance parameter BR_B by a factor of 1.2 in both directions. This increases the line charging susceptance between bus 14 and bus 70 by 20% relative to its original value.

After applying these modifications, run an ACOPF using MATPOWER with the OPF violation tolerance parameter `opf.violation` set to 1e-6, and print the resulting power flow and optimization summary.

Perform an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 9-bus test system (case9). Before solving, modify the quadratic active power cost coefficient of the generator connected at bus 3 by scaling it to 80% of its original value. Concretely, multiply the third-order cost coefficient (the quadratic term in the generator cost function) for all generators located at bus 3 by a factor of 0.8, leaving all other cost parameters and network data unchanged. Use an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-6 when running the ACOPF.

Formulate and solve an AC optimal power flow problem for the MATPOWER microgrid test system case33mg. First, reduce the active power demand at bus 18 by scaling its original active load by a factor of 0.9, thereby decreasing the real power consumption at that bus by 10%. Next, modify the reactive power capability of the generator connected to bus 1 by setting its minimum reactive power output limit to -50 MVAr, allowing it to absorb up to 50 MVAr of reactive power. Then, adjust the resistance of the transmission branch that electrically connects bus 14 and bus 22 by multiplying its original series resistance value by 1.1, increasing the branch resistance by 10% in both directions of power flow (14–22 and 22–14). After these network parameter changes, solve the AC optimal power flow on the modified case33mg system using an OPF violation tolerance of 1e-7, and print the resulting power flow and optimal dispatch report.

Run an AC optimal power flow (ACOPF) on the modified case9Q system. First, adjust the reactive power demand at bus 2 by increasing it by 10%, i.e., scale the reactive power demand at bus 2 by a factor of 1.1. Then tighten the upper voltage magnitude limit at bus 1 by scaling its maximum allowable voltage magnitude by a factor of 1.02 relative to its original value. For the transmission element connecting bus 6 and bus 4, enforce the in-service status by setting its branch status flag to 1, treating this line as fully in service in both directions (6–4 and 4–6 if present). Finally, solve the ACOPF with an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) set to 1e-7.

Run an AC optimal power flow on the IEEE 118-bus test system (case118). Before solving, modify the network data as follows. At bus 59, scale the maximum allowable bus voltage magnitude (VMAX) by a factor of 1.05, thereby increasing the upper voltage limit at that specific bus by 5% relative to its original value. For the generator located at bus 12, increase the generator’s maximum reactive power output limit (QMAX) by multiplying its original value by 1.2, effectively raising its reactive power capability at that bus by 20%. Use an OPF violation tolerance (opf.violation) of 1e-6 in the MATPOWER options, then execute the ACOPF and print the resulting power flow and OPF solution report.
